recognize_zh: 同一抹片中嗜中性球、嗜酸性球（橘紅顆粒）與嗜鹼性球（深紫粗顆粒）都出現核分葉過多（多於 5 葉），三種顆粒球系列同時受影響，符合羥基脲（hydroxycarbamide）引起的巨母紅血球樣變化。
features: Panels A–C: eosinophils with orange-red granules and nuclei divided into 4–6 or more lobes (normal eosinophils are bilobed)
Panels D–F: basophils with coarse dark purple-black granules partly obscuring nuclei that appear multilobated
Panels G–I: neutrophils with 6 or more distinct nuclear lobes connected by thin filaments (hypersegmentation)
Background red cells mildly macrocytic/oval with occasional stomatocyte-like forms
Granulocyte cytoplasm and granulation otherwise normal; no Döhle bodies or toxic granulation
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows nuclear hypersegmentation affecting all three granulocytic lineages. Neutrophils contain six or more lobes, eosinophils show four to six lobes instead of the normal bilobed configuration, and basophils have multilobated nuclei partially obscured by coarse granules. Red cells appear mildly macrocytic with some oval forms, and cytoplasmic granulation is otherwise normal. Findings are consistent with drug-induced megaloblastoid change due to hydroxycarbamide (hydroxyurea), although vitamin B12/folate deficiency should be excluded.

ddx.vs: Morphology is identical, so distinction relies on serum B12/folate, methylmalonic acid/homocysteine and drug history.
The inherited trait affects neutrophils only, without macrocytosis, and persists without drug exposure.
MDS more often shows hypolobated (pseudo-Pelger) and hypogranular neutrophils with cytopenias and clonal abnormalities rather than uniform hypersegmentation across all granulocytes.
Iron deficiency can cause mild neutrophil hypersegmentation but with microcytic hypochromic red cells rather than macrocytes.
